slides.label: THE MOCK EXAMPLE
lines: Meet Sample Ridge Outfitters again. Still not a real business.
A hunter lands on the homepage and decides in seconds whether to keep reading. Here's what has to be on screen before they scroll.

slides.label: ABOVE THE FOLD 1 · WHAT DO YOU DO?
items: The mock homepage
A banner that says “Welcome.” You have to scroll to learn it's a guided elk hunt.
The fix
One plain line at the top: guided elk hunts in [your state], and the species and seasons you offer.

slides.label: ABOVE THE FOLD 2 · A REAL PHOTO
items: The mock homepage
A stock photo of mountains. Could be anyone's.
The fix
A real hunter, real camp, real elk. Your own photo says you're a working operation.

slides.label: ABOVE THE FOLD 3 · WHAT NEXT?
items: The mock homepage
A menu with eight links and no button. The phone number is in the footer.
The fix
One clear button (“Check 2027 dates”) and your phone number, both on the first screen.

slides.label: ABOVE THE FOLD 4 · ON A PHONE
items: The mock homepage
On a phone, the logo fills the screen and the headline is below the fold.
The fix
Open it on your own phone. If the headline and the button aren't both visible, shrink the logo.

slides.label: YOUR 1-MINUTE CHECK
slides.title: Open your homepage on your phone
items: Can you tell what you offer without scrolling?
Is the photo yours?
Is there one button and a phone number?
Do the dates or booking info show up in one tap?

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: Most hunters find you on their phone, often through Google.
If the first screen answers what, where and how to book, they keep going. If not, they back out and try the next outfitter.
